title: Embedded Systems Emulator — Overview and definition
t: Embedded Systems Emulator — Overview and definition
description: Runs firmware against emulated CPUs and peripherals before hardware exists.
body: Signature edition. Signature-original methods and framings for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout. Runs firmware against emulated CPUs and peripherals before hardware exists. An embedded systems emulator executes MCU firmware on an emulated core with virtual UART, timers, GPIO, ADC, and flash, catching crashes and logic bugs without a board. Real implementations include QEMU (ARM/RISC-V system mode), Renode (multi-node with peripherals), and SimAVR for AVR parts. It supports deterministic replay, fault injection, and virtual wiring between emulated nodes.
capabilities: Emulate ARM Cortex-M, RISC-V, AVR, and MSP430 cores
Virtual peripherals: UART, SPI, I2C, timers, ADC, Ethernet
Deterministic execution with record/replay of inputs
Multi-node virtual wiring for distributed firmware testing
Fault injection: bit flips, bus faults, and peripheral failures

title: Embedded Systems Emulator — Actual implementation
description: Runs firmware against emulated CPUs and peripherals before hardware exists.
body: Signature edition. Signature-original methods and framings for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout. How Embedded Systems Emulator is actually implemented. An embedded systems emulator executes MCU firmware on an emulated core with virtual UART, timers, GPIO, ADC, and flash, catching crashes and logic bugs without a board. Real implementations combine CLI, Python scripting API (Renode), GDB stub for debugging with A JIT/TCG engine (QEMU), peripheral models, Python for scripting. The implementation is verified by Verify by running a reference firmware test suite in the emulator: all assertions pass and UART output matches the golden log byte-for-byte

title: Embedded Systems Emulator — Teaching-ladder exercise
description: Runs firmware against emulated CPUs and peripherals before hardware exists.
body: Signature edition. Signature-original methods and framings for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout. Teaching ladder for Embedded Systems Emulator, simple to complex. Rank 1: name the tool's single core action (Emulate ARM Cortex-M, RISC-V, AVR, and MSP430 cores). Rank 3: run it once on a tiny input and check the output. Rank 5: combine two capabilities: Emulate ARM Cortex-M, RISC-V, AVR, and MSP430 cores and Virtual peripherals: UART, SPI, I2C, timers, ADC, Ethernet. Rank 7: chain its output into a neighboring tool (Microcontroller programming environment) with a verification checkpoint. Rank 9+: automate the full workflow and teach it to someone else.
